items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: Uh, and we went to meet him at the other main railroad station at night.

ctx.x: Well, there's, yeah, I think there's some, I think it's, most people seem to think that this was in 1931. The Friday died. Because I think that, that was the year Loi Armstrong was down there was in 31. I think he came down here twice. I mean, he came down here twice.

I was 31. He came down here twice. I mean, the first time he came down here, Keenan Fender was very popular. And, uh, had a saxophone player with a thing. I never saw him. All I could hear him say, hold it out. They hold that one note, which is, uh, Andrew Martin. And, uh, the next time he came down here was in the 30s. I know it was in the 30s because I was living, uh, 1215 McGlondon Street. Uh, and we went to meet him at the other main railroad station at night. And, uh, I was in the morning, up to the…

Now, which of these two times was the time that Buddy died? I think it was the first time. Yes. That's my idea. I'm sure it was the first time. Well, I could, we could easily find out what those two times was that Buddy came down because it would be, you know, somewhere rather written down or something. But, um, I guess 31 is what they normally think that Buddy was when he died. No, I don't think there's any.
